obtained.how: institutional open copy: SORA (Searchable Ornithological Research Archive) at Digital Commons @ University of South Florida, PDF fetched with curl and getsrc's honest user agent (getsrc itself got 403 from the same URL), indexed with getsrc --file; the text layer is partly garbled (doubled letters), so the results page and Table 2 were read on the page images

bibliography.checked_against: the article's pages and the USF Digital Commons record
bibliography.note: Kees Vermeer, 'Some aspects of the nesting requirements of common loons in Alberta', Wilson Bulletin 85(4): 429-435 (December 1973). The DOI in the ledger (10.5281/zenodo.16171389) is Plazi's 2025 Zenodo re-deposit of the BHL scan; the stable open copy is https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/wilson_bulletin/vol85/iss4/3 (BHL part 209307 is behind a Cloudflare check for scripts).

claims.claim: Of 26 nests in one study none lay more than about 1.2 m from water (Vermeer 1973)
claims.location: p. 431 (PDF p. 4), Results (Nest Sites); p. 432 (PDF p. 5), Table 2
claims.quote: none was more than four feet away from a lake
claims.conditions: 4 ft = 1.22 m, distance of nest rim to water; 26 nests found (of 33 breeding pairs) on 19 road-accessible, eutrophic, sport-fished Alberta lakes up to 3,000 acres, surveyed in 1972; Table 2: 15 nests at 0 ft, 6 at 0.1-1.0, 2 at 1.1-2.0, 1 at 2.1-3.0, 2 at 3.1-4.0 ft; 25 of the 26 nests were on islands
claims.note: Most nests (15 of 26) were right at the water's edge.

claims.claim: loons nest within about 1.2 m of the water (Vermeer 1973; Section 3.8)
claims.location: p. 431 (PDF p. 4), Results; p. 432 (PDF p. 5), Table 2
claims.quote: Most loon nests were situated directly on the waters' edge and none was
claims.conditions: one Alberta study, 26 nests in 1972 (as above); the general statement rests on this single sample
claims.note: Fair as a generalisation if the sentence keeps the citation; 'in one Alberta study of 26 nests' would make the basis plain.

notes: Other values: 20 nests were sheltered in a bay or by a nearby island, 6 faced open water; 19 of 25 island nests were on islands under 2 acres (preference not significant); in 25 cases the nest gave a good underwater exit. The author cites a Saskatchewan lake where 10 of 25 nests were washed out by high water and boat waves (personal communication) — relevant to the paper's water-level point.
